open_points.subject: Authored trial-case file fixtures
open_points.text: `functions.add_trial_case` takes “input values by port, optional expected outputs”, while “a check is given a file as facts — digest, size, media type — never bytes” and the operation must publish fixture bytes through `store.put_value_bytes`.
open_points.question: How do the bytes of authored input and expected-output file fixtures enter `functions.add_trial_case`, and which caller computes and verifies their file facts before they are stored?
options: The surface passes bytes together with computed facts to `functions.add_trial_case`.
The surface publishes the bytes first and passes a StoredValue reference.
A separate file-upload operation stages fixture bytes before the case is added.
open_points.default_guess: Pass fixture bytes and facts to `functions.add_trial_case`; let it publish them only after all case checks pass.

open_points.subject: Actors of automatic records inside caller-triggered operations
open_points.text: “Every operation that writes a record receives the acting Actor M27 … from its caller”, but submission writes TrialExecutions, an AdmissionVerdict and a kernel Activation, and “the kernel” is the actor of admission and automatic activation.
open_points.question: For each record produced inside `submit_implementation`, `try_implementation`, run advancement and effect processing, is the recorded actor the request actor or the kernel, especially for record models that currently name no actor?
options: Use the request actor for requested records and the kernel for automatic executions, verdicts and activations.
Use the request actor for the whole operation except activations explicitly assigned to the kernel.
Treat observation records as actorless and record actors only in fields already named by State 1.
open_points.default_guess: Record the request actor for the submitted implementation or explicit trial, and the kernel for automatic admission evidence, verdicts, activations and execution observations.

open_points.subject: Refusal-reason size handling
open_points.text: State 5 says, “A refusal's reason is at most `bounded_text_bytes_max`, cut at a UTF-8 character boundary,” while A20 says, “Over a ceiling is always a refusal or a failure, never a truncation … The one exception is `failure_detail`.”
open_points.question: May refusal reasons be truncated, or must every possible reason be constructed so it is already within the bound?
options: Permit truncation of refusal reasons as an additional explicit exception.
Require bounded reason templates and bounded substitutions so truncation never occurs.
Return only a fixed reason identifier when the explanatory text would exceed the bound.
open_points.default_guess: Use bounded reason templates and never truncate a refusal reason.

open_points.subject: Filtered cursor pagination over mutable records
open_points.text: The token is “the store position of the last item returned; the next page starts below it,” but “a record whose filtered field (a status) changes between pages leaves or enters the pages still to come.”
open_points.question: What happens when a record above the continuation position did not match the first page's status filter but changes to a matching status before the next page, or a previously returned record stops matching?
options: Use live filtering and accept that matching changes above the cursor are not returned.
Snapshot filter membership when the first page is issued.
Restart or invalidate pagination when a filtered lifecycle field changes.
open_points.default_guess: Use live filtering below the cursor and explicitly state that changes above the cursor are outside the remaining traversal.

open_points.subject: Repair-view continuation token
open_points.text: The `get_repair_view` token “also carries the implementation set of its first page”, while every other request string is bounded by `bounded_text_bytes_max` and a slot may have an unbounded implementation history.
open_points.question: How is an arbitrarily large first-page implementation set represented in a bounded, stateless continuation token?
options: Store server-side cursor state and put only its identifier in the token.
Represent the set by a store-position cutoff and derive it again on later pages.
Impose a bound on the number of implementations eligible for the repair view.
Allow the token to exceed the normal bounded-text limit.
open_points.default_guess: Encode a stable store-position cutoff and rederive the implementation set from records at or below that cutoff.

open_points.subject: Run outputs and their source of truth
open_points.text: `record_run_progress` writes “the run's status, outputs, WaitingPoints”, but `runs.read_run` says the answer is “computed from the trace when asked, never stored”; recovery explicitly rewrites lagging status and waiting points but does not say whether it rewrites lagging outputs.
open_points.question: Are produced run outputs persisted fields of Run M19, a derived view of the trace, or a persisted cache; and if cached, how are discrepancies and crash-lagged outputs repaired?
options: Derive outputs solely from immutable trace records and do not store them on Run.
Persist outputs on Run as authoritative fields.
Persist outputs as a cache and rebuild them with status and waiting points during recovery.
open_points.default_guess: Treat the trace as authoritative and persist Run outputs only as a cache that recovery rebuilds.

open_points.subject: Agent-visible effect approval previews
open_points.text: An approval preview contains “the built request” including the full URL, JSON body or multipart description, while “an agent never receives a `personal_data` value” and State 5 only specifies masking values and files resolved from records.
open_points.question: How is an approval preview returned to an agent when personal-data inputs have been embedded in its URL, query parameters, JSON body or multipart value parts?
options: Return only `request_digest` and a redacted structural description to agents.
Omit the whole request description from agent responses.
Replace each derived personal-data occurrence with its digest and class while preserving the rest of the request description.
Make approvals and their previews owner-readable only.
open_points.default_guess: Return the request digest and a structural preview with every personal-data-derived component replaced by digest and class.

open_points.subject: Credential-reference resolution
open_points.text: `installation.resolve_service_credential` resolves “the reference that resolves to its value on the host”; A17 mentions a “secret file” that may be missing or unreadable, but no reference syntax, byte encoding, maximum size, file-safety rule or value normalization is fixed.
open_points.question: What exactly is a credential reference, how is it resolved, and which file, encoding, size, symlink, permission and newline rules determine `credential_unresolved`?
options: An absolute path to a private regular UTF-8 file whose complete contents are the header value.
A reference interpreted by a defined host secret-store provider.
A tagged reference supporting a closed set of file and secret-store schemes.
open_points.default_guess: Use an absolute path to a private, non-symlink regular file; read a bounded UTF-8 value verbatim and reject empty values or any control character.

open_points.subject: Manifest revision pinning
open_points.text: `manifest_source` returns a “manifest location and revision fixed at start”, and A08 concludes that “a record changes for a running kernel only after a restart with a new configured revision”, although bindings reread files from the manifest location before sends.
open_points.question: How does the kernel resolve and pin `manifest_revision` so edits at the same filesystem location cannot change what a running process reads?
options: Read manifest files directly from an immutable repository object identified by the revision.
Load and retain a complete manifest snapshot at startup.
Trust an external deployment rule that the configured directory never changes during a process lifetime.
open_points.default_guess: Resolve the revision to an immutable repository snapshot and read every manifest record from that snapshot.

open_points.subject: Store creation and first start
open_points.text: `store.open_store` takes a data directory and checks locking, privacy and links, while A18 says the directory “holds one SQLite database” and several subareas; no text says whether a missing directory, database, schema or subdirectory is created or refused.
open_points.question: What does `store.open_store` do on a first installation or when some expected store components do not yet exist?
options: Require a separately initialized complete store and refuse anything missing.
Create the database and internal directories inside an existing private data directory.
Create the data directory and the complete store layout itself.
Use explicit store schema versions and migrations for missing or older layouts.
open_points.default_guess: Require the configured private data directory to exist, then atomically create a new versioned database and internal subdirectories when it is empty.

open_points.subject: HTTP base URL parsing and joining
open_points.text: An `api_base_url` is accepted when it is “an absolute `http` or `https` URL with a host”, and the request URL is “the `api_base_url` without a trailing `/` followed by the declared path”; query strings, fragments, user information, repeated trailing slashes and existing base paths are not addressed.
open_points.question: Which base-URL forms are valid, and what exact parsing and joining rule produces the request URL and `host` header for every accepted form?
options: Restrict the base URL to scheme, authority and an optional normalized path, with no user information, query or fragment.
Perform literal removal of one trailing slash and string concatenation for every otherwise valid absolute URL.
Use a specified URL-library resolution algorithm and canonicalization rules.
open_points.default_guess: Reject user information, query and fragment; allow an optional base path and define literal removal of all trailing path slashes before appending the declared path.

open_points.subject: Service error `failure_detail`
open_points.text: For an error response, “at most `failure_detail_bytes_max` of it is kept as `failure_detail`”, but the text does not say which bytes are selected, how arbitrary non-UTF-8 bodies are represented, or how the guarantee that credentials never enter a failure detail is enforced.
open_points.question: How is `failure_detail` deterministically derived from an arbitrary service error body while remaining valid bounded text and excluding the resolved credential value?
options: Keep a UTF-8-safe prefix after replacing exact credential occurrences.
Keep no service response body, only a fixed outcome description.
Encode a bounded byte prefix in a textual representation after secret filtering.
Keep a digest and byte length instead of an excerpt.
open_points.default_guess: Produce a UTF-8-safe prefix after removing exact occurrences of the resolved credential, and fall back to a digest and length for non-text bodies.
